ticket_text: Hi, I just published my first chatbot app and I want to call it from my own backend. Where do I get an API key for it? -- Marcus
assistant_answer: Hi Marcus, congrats on publishing your first app! You can get the key from inside that app: open the app in Studio, go to API Access (sometimes labeled Monitoring > API Key), and click 'Create new Secret Key.' Copy it right away since Dify only shows it once -- the key is prefixed app- and you'll use it as a Bearer token in the Authorization header when calling the app's API. Note that this key only works for this specific app; if you publish a second app later you'll need to generate a separate key for it.

ticket_text: How do I connect my own OpenAI API key instead of using the built-in credits? I don't want to burn through my free trial too fast. -- Priya

From that point on, calls using OpenAI models are billed directly by OpenAI with your key, and they won't draw down your Dify message credits at all.

ticket_text: What's the difference between the chunking options when I upload a document to my knowledge base? I see General, Parent-Child, and Q&A and I don't know which to pick. -- Felix
assistant_answer: Hi Felix, here's the quick breakdown: General splits your document into fixed-size segments with some overlap -- good as a default for most content. Parent-Child embeds a smaller child chunk for matching but returns its larger parent chunk to the model, which helps when you want tight retrieval matches but fuller context in the answer. Q&A auto-generates question/answer pairs from your source text, which works well for FAQ-style documents. For a general product manual like yours, I'd start with General chunking and switch to Parent-Child if you notice answers feel like they're missing surrounding context.

ticket_text: What's the difference between Economical and High Quality indexing when I set up a dataset? Does it matter which I pick? -- Lena
assistant_answer: Hi Lena, it matters mainly for cost and retrieval quality. Economical indexing is keyword-based, free, and doesn't count against your plan's Knowledge Data Storage quota. High Quality indexing uses vector embeddings through your workspace's embedding model, which generally gives better semantic retrieval, but it does consume your Knowledge Data Storage allowance and will stop accepting new documents once that quota is full. If you're on Sandbox or Professional and expect a large knowledge base, keep an eye on your storage usage if you choose High Quality.

ticket_text: I'm getting a 401 Unauthorized when I try to call the dataset API to upload a document, but the same key works fine for my chatbot app. What's going on? -- Sam
assistant_answer: Hi Sam, that's expected behavior, not a bug: app API keys and dataset (knowledge base) API keys are separate and not interchangeable. The key from your chatbot app's API Access panel only authenticates calls to that app's endpoint. For the dataset API, you need a key created from the dataset's own detail page, under its Service API panel -- that key is scoped to that knowledge base specifically. Create a dataset key there and swap it into your upload request; your app key won't work for that endpoint.

ticket_text: My retrieval node sometimes returns way more context than I expect, and other times almost nothing. What settings control that? -- Felix
assistant_answer: Hi Felix, two settings on the retrieval node control that: top_k sets the maximum number of chunks returned, and the score threshold (if enabled) discards any chunk scoring below that cutoff even if it would otherwise be within top_k. If you're seeing too much context, try lowering top_k or raising the score threshold; if you're seeing almost nothing back, your threshold may be set too high for how your embeddings are scoring, or the query simply isn't matching much in the dataset. You can use Hit Testing on the dataset to try different queries and see the actual scores before tuning further.
